text.insert: HarnessState is the durable coordination record for one game. It owns dispatch authority, queued requests, blockers, and event provenance. The dashboard composes cycle, run, sync, and knowledge summaries into a separate HarnessStateView.

Cycle, run, sync, and knowledge payloads remain in their domain stores. They are not nested fields in the stored HarnessState record. The current dashboard projection returns pr: null in its compatibility read model and pr_work: [] in HarnessStateView.
At most one workflow holds active_workflow for a game. The lease kind vocabulary retains run, pr, and sync. A queued request grants no authority.
owns acquisition, fencing, settlement, and recovery.

The lease carries workflow_id, lease_id, status, acquisition and heartbeat times, blockers, and an optional requested_handoff. A handoff uses target_kind and target_workflow_id plus the request lineage. Null active_workflow means authority is free, even when domain workflow records remain readable.

owns HarnessStateView and its 13-action inventory. The view exposes harness_revision from the stored coordination revision. Domain objects keep their own revisions; this is not a single version field copied onto every child state.

Accepted coordination changes record event provenance with the state transition. created_at and updated_at preserve record timing. caused_by_event_id may be null at initialization, so reconstruction must not invent an accepted event for that initial value.
